story.title: Congo Receives Over 16,000 Doses of Ebola Vaccine Amid Severe Outbreak
story.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo has received more than 16,000 doses of the Ervebo vaccine as it confronts the deadliest Ebola outbreak in its history. The shipment arrived late Friday, providing critical support in the ongoing health crisis.

timeline_highlights.title: Ebola Outbreak in DRC Expands to Sixth Province Amid Rising Death Toll
timeline_highlights.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has now spread to a sixth province, Bas-Uele, following the death of a man who traveled from Haut-Uele. The World Health Organization has indicated that this outbreak is on track to become the deadliest in history, surpassing the previous record of over 11,000 fatalities from a decade ago. Currently, more than 2,100 deaths have been reported out of over 4,500 cases.

event_overview.title: About Congo Ebola Outbreak
event_overview.subject: Congo Ebola Outbreak
event_overview.summary: The 2026 Congo Ebola outbreak is an ongoing epidemic of Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD), first declared by the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda on May 15, 2026. It is centered in eastern DR Congo, where transmission expanded rapidly amid conflict, population movement, and limits on health-system access; WHO has classified the event as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern.

facts.label: Start and status
facts.value: The health ministries of DR Congo and Uganda declared outbreaks of Bundibugyo virus disease on May 15, 2026. As of August 21, 2026, the outbreak remained active in DR Congo; Uganda had declared its outbreak over on July 28 after 42 days without a new locally transmitted case.

facts.label: Disease agent
facts.value: The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo virus, a species that causes Ebola disease. WHO reported that no licensed Bundibugyo-virus-specific vaccine or therapeutic was available, although candidate countermeasures were being developed and assessed.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: The epidemic began in Ituri Province and had spread to six DR Congo provinces by August 13: Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uélé, Tshopo, and an additional province reported in WHO's August risk assessment. Ituri remained the epicentre.

facts.label: Scale
facts.value: WHO's August 20 risk assessment reported 4,566 confirmed cases and 2,128 deaths in DR Congo as of August 13, 2026. Reported totals can change through delayed reporting, expanded testing, and reconciliation of earlier records.

facts.label: International framework and response
facts.value: On May 17, 2026, the WHO Director-General determined that the DR Congo–Uganda event constituted a Public Health Emergency of International Concern under the International Health Regulations. The response centers on surveillance, contact tracing, laboratory testing, infection prevention and control, clinical care, community engagement, and cross-border preparedness.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline highlights major developments from July 22 through August 11, 2026; it does not provide a complete case ledger, every local response measure, or all cross-border and international updates.

related_stories.summary: A sword attack at a high school in Fagersta, central Sweden, resulted in one death and three injuries. The victim was a 17-year-old girl. An 18-year-old male suspect has been arrested following the incident, which occurred as schools reopened in the area. Police are investigating potential online influences that may have incited the attack.

related_stories.title: Supreme Court Temporarily Allows Construction of $400 Million White House Ballroom
related_stories.summary: The US Supreme Court has granted a temporary order allowing the continuation of construction on a $400 million ballroom at the White House, a project associated with President Donald Trump. This decision comes after lower courts had previously ordered a halt to the work, citing the need for congressional approval. The ruling provides a temporary victory for the Trump administration as it navigates ongoing legal challenges regarding the renovation.

related_stories.title: Pentagon Dismisses Leadership of Stars and Stripes Amid Editorial Independence Concerns
related_stories.summary: The Pentagon has dismissed the editor-in-chief, publisher, and a reporter of Stars and Stripes, citing insubordination. The firings occurred after the editor and reporter publicly opposed potential editorial interference from the Defense Department. This action raises concerns about the independence of the military news outlet, which has a history of editorial autonomy.
